content:
**Fixed scalar() reading trailing space as a value (#612)**

**What**: Changed `scalar(block, key)` in `brain/scripts/review/lib/yaml-block.mjs` from `^${key}:[ \t]*(.+)$` to `^${key}:[ \t]*(\S.*)$`. `[ \t]*` and `.trim()` are unchanged on purpose.
**Why**: A key line carrying only trailing whitespace (`key: `, `key:\t`) used to backtrack `(.+)` into the whitespace, trim it to `''`, and be read as a PRESENT-but-empty value instead of the ABSENT state — this silently dropped `findings:`/`follow_ups:` entry lists on `parse-verdict.mjs` whenever the emitted key line happened to carry a trailing space.
**Where**: `brain/scripts/review/lib/yaml-block.mjs` (fix), `yaml-block.test.mjs` (new, boundary table), `parse-verdict.test.mjs` (F2 pin rewritten in place), `actor-check.test.mjs`, `decision-block.test.mjs`, `epic-map.test.mjs`, `checkpoint-block.test.mjs` (consumer pins), `yaml-block.drift.test.mjs` (header comment only).
**Learned**: (1) `\s*` is a trap here — under the `/m` flag it eats `\n` and lets the capture bleed into the next line, reconstructing a worse version of the bug; also JS `\s` (no `u` flag) matches U+00A0 NBSP per the ECMAScript WhiteSpace production, so `\s*` would re-admit NBSP through the prefix too. (2) The NBSP row (`key: <NBSP>v` → `null`) is the ONLY row that kills the `(\S.*)`→`(.*)` mutant — `.trim()` strips NBSP so a naive `(.*)`+trim silently re-admits it. (3) When mutation-testing an uncommitted fix, commit the fix FIRST — `git checkout --` used to restore from a mutant will revert all the way to the last commit, silently discarding an uncommitted real fix along with the mutant.
